<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In premature infants, successful ex utero maturation depends on endogenous and exogenous stimuli. Chemical insults during this period may impact long-term development. Given immature hepatic biotransformation, parenteral xenobiotic exposure may be of particular toxicological relevance. We conducted a single-center case study to characterize the xenobiotic burden of neonatal parenteral nutrition (PN). A standardized PN regimen for a 28-week, 1000 g reference infant was passed through infusion lines and the flow-through analyzed via a multianalyte exposome LC-MS/MS assay. Eighteen of 221 targeted xenobiotics were detected. Diisononyl phthalate (DINP, 780 ng/mL), bisphenol A (BPA, 250 ng/mL), methylparaben (MP, 74 ng/mL), and 5-hydroxymethyl-2-furanoic acid (HMFA, 43 ng/mL) showed the highest mean concentrations. The estimated daily intake of BPA (9.5 μg/kg bw/d) exceeded calculated and official Health-Based Guidance Values. Consistent with immature detoxification, pharmacokinetic modeling suggested accumulation of DINP, MINP, and free BPA in premature infants. The higher predicted exposure of premature infants to free BPA warrants investigation into 4-methyl-2,4-bis(4-hydroxyphenyl)pent-1-ene (MBP) formation under potentially saturated Phase II metabolism. An exploratory analysis of plasma data from extremely premature infants indicated PN as a contributory rather than predominant source of intervention-related exposure. These findings represent a relevant clinical reference scenario rather than a population-wide exposure estimate.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>In this study, a long-term atmospheric observation of HFC-23, -32, -125, -134a, -143a, and -152a was conducted at six background stations across China from 2011 to 2023. Using a tracer ratio method with HCFC-22 as the reference, emissions from four main economic regions, Northeast Plain (NEP), North China Plain (NCP), Yangtze River Delta (YRD), and Central South China (CSC), were estimated, and their trends were analyzed over four phases: Phase 1 (2012–2016), Phase 2 (2017–2018), Phase 3 (2019–2020), and Phase 4 (2021–2023). The results show that from 2011 to 2023, the atmospheric mixing ratios of all studied HFCs except HFC-152a exhibited increasing trends. Nationally, emissions of HFC-23 show a decreasing tendency during Phase 4, while emissions of HFC-32, -125, -134a, and -143a continued to rise throughout Phases 3 and 4. These four HFCs were identified as the dominant species, accounting for over 76% of total HFCs’ mass emissions. From Phase 3 to Phase 4, CO2-equivalent HFC emissions per capita increased slightly, whereas emissions per unit GDP decreased, which is mainly attributable to significant HFC reductions in the CSC region. Nevertheless, China’s average HFC emission intensities (whether calculated per unit GDP or per capita) remain approximately 1.5–1.6 times the global average.</jats:p>

title:
Role of Coordination
Environment in the Oxidation
of CrIII Aminocarboxylate Complexes by Hydrous Manganese
Oxide
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Oxidation of CrIII to CrVI by MnIII,IV (hydr)oxides plays an important role in controlling chromium mobility and toxicity in soils and sediments. Previous studies on CrIII oxidation by hydrous manganese oxide (HMO) reveals that reaction rates are highly sensitive to CrIII speciation, with aminocarboxylate complexes exhibiting reaction-induced Mn2+ accumulation at HMO surfaces, which progressively inhibits CrVI production. In this work, we compare initial CrVI production rates for well-defined, presynthesized CrIII–aminocarboxylate complexes with the chelating agents iminodiacetic acid (IDA), nitrilotriacetic acid (NTA), N-(2-hydroxyethyl)ethylenediaminetriacetic acid (HEDTA), and ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA). Initial-rate measurements minimize the influence of secondary ligand oxidation, reaction-generated MnII, and associated changes in HMO reactivity, thereby providing a common basis for comparing the effects of CrIII coordination environment. Initial CrVI production rates spanned 8 orders of magnitude and generally decrease as aminocarboxylate ligands occupy a greater fraction of the CrIII coordination sphere and fewer coordination positions remain occupied by H2O and OH–. These results demonstrate that CrIII oxidation by Mn oxides is acutely sensitive to the CrIII coordination environment, with important implications for CrVI formation in natural and engineered systems. These findings demonstrate that meaningful prediction of CrVI formation requires explicit consideration of CrIII speciation.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Gas hydrates can form when water and a guest gas coexist within the hydrate stability field. Gas hydrates in porous rocks block flow fields. During CO2 storage in depleted reservoirs, pressure reduction and Joule–Thomson cooling may place near-well regions within the CO2 hydrate stability zone, raising concerns about injectivity loss. Hydrate stability is commonly inferred from the bulk pressure–temperature (P–T) phase diagram, which neglects flow and gas humidity transport under sustained flow. Using time-resolved optical microscopy in a “fish-bone” micromodel at fixed P and T, we find that injecting low-humidity CO2 produces a pore-scale cycle of hydrate formation and dissociation. The hydrate nucleates along gas–water–solid contact lines and grows by consuming CO2 dissolved in trapped pore water and then slows as CO2 supply becomes diffusion-limited through the hydrate layer. Despite constant bulk P and T, the low humidity of the injected CO2 extracts water as vapor, creating a water chemical potential deficit at the gas–hydrate interface and driving an inlet-to-outlet dissociation front. These results show that hydrate persistence under flow depends on pore-scale transport and gas-side water chemical potential and cannot be inferred from bulk P–T stability conditions alone.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Novel organophosphate esters (OPEs), formed through chemical transformation of commercial antioxidants, are emerging contaminants with widespread environmental occurrence and potential health effects. Despite their widespread detection, the atmospheric reactivity, persistence, and transformation of novel OPEs remain unknown. Here, the heterogeneous OH oxidation of two surface-bound novel OPEs [tris(2,4-ditert-butylphenyl) phosphate (TDtBPP) and triisodecyl phosphate (TiDeP)] was explored by investigating the reaction kinetics and chemical mechanisms. The measured heterogeneous rate constants for TDtBPP and TiDeP were (2.81 ± 0.12) × 10–12 and (1.99 ± 0.16) × 10–12 cm3 molecules–1 s–1, respectively, equivalent to atmospheric lifetimes of up to 6.3 and 9.0 days. These lifetimes are significantly longer than previously predicted values (&lt;1 day), suggesting that they are much more persistent in air than predicted. Based on UPLC-HRMS measurements, 22 transformation products from the heterogeneous reactions were identified for the first time. Analysis of atmospheric particle samples from two megacities in China identified four TDtBPP transformation products, demonstrating that the oxidation chemistry can occur under genuine environmental conditions. In-silico hazard screening further indicated that many transformation products may be more bioaccumulative and more toxic than the parent novel OPEs. The results not only provide new insights into the atmospheric persistence of novel OPEs but also underscore the significance of considering atmospheric transformation in the risk assessment of these emerging contaminants.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The biological mechanisms linking air pollution to lung carcinogenesis remain underexplored. This study aimed to identify key proteins and pathways involved in mediating the effects of air pollutants on lung cancer risk. We analyzed 95 matched lung cancer case–control pairs of ever-smokers with prediagnosis plasma protein profiles measured in the Cancer Prevention Study-II Nutrition Cohort. We assessed associations between protein levels and six individual air pollutants, air pollution mixture, and lung cancer risk, adjusting for confounders and multiple testing. We identified overlapping proteins and enriched pathways associated with both exposures and lung cancer risk, followed by an exploratory high-dimensional mediation analysis (HIMA) to investigate the potential mediating roles of proteins. Seventeen proteins were associated with both exposures and lung cancer, including CX3CL1, ADAM15, and CXCL17 (P &lt; 0.05). HIMA identified six proteins, including CX3CL1 and CXCL17, as potential mediating proteins of individual pollutant-lung cancer associations (Bonferroni-corrected P &lt; 0.05), while these findings did not remain significant when excluding cases diagnosed within one year of blood draw. The exploratory results suggest that proteins and pathways related to inflammatory chemokine signaling, immune modulation, and altered cell proliferation, migration, and survival may play significant roles in air pollution-lung cancer association among ever-smokers.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Atmospheric elemental mercury (Hg0) emitted from the nonferrous metallurgy industry poses severe risks to ecosystems. Although metal sulfides are promising in Hg0 adsorption under high-concentration SO2 conditions, they typically suffer from poor performance at elevated temperatures due to weak binding affinity. Herein, a trivalent iron (Fe3+) activation strategy to boost Hg0 adsorption activity of metal sulfides was developed for the first time, which leverages electron-deficient Fe3+ to induce electronic reconstruction. This Fe3+ activation strategy is applicable to various metal sulfides, generating Fe sites with high activity and stability. Among the various candidates, the Fe3+-activated MoS2 delivers a record-theoretical saturated Hg0 adsorption capacity of 69.56 mg·g–1 at 150 °C, which is 4.35 times higher than that of pristine MoS2. The sulfur vacancies on MoS2 serve as the key anchoring sites for Fe3+, generating stable single-atom, dimer, and trimer Fe configurations. These new Fe centers, benefiting from charge modulation, can simultaneously adsorb two Hg atoms via charge transfer and orbital hybridization. The Fe3+-activated MoS2 exhibits strong resistance to SO2 and H2O, maintaining high Hg0 removal efficiency under a smelting gas atmosphere. This work reveals new configurations of Hg adsorption and provides a convenient route to design high-performance sorbents for heavy metal purification.</jats:p>

title:
Divergent Responses
of Manganese Oxides to Olivine
Dissolution and Their Control on Trace Metal Fates under an Ocean
Alkalinity Enhancement Scenario
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Olivine-based ocean alkalinity enhancement (OAE) is a promising carbon dioxide removal technology; however, the geochemical fate of olivine-derived toxic metals, particularly nickel (Ni) and chromium (Cr) at marine sediment interfaces, remains poorly constrained. We employed dialysis-membrane microcosms to isolate olivine from Mn oxides, allowing only dissolved species to diffuse and react under three olivine loadings (1, 5, and 10 g L–1) in seawater for 60 days. Results revealed that (1) Ni was preferentially sequestered by the Mn oxides, with δ-MnO2 showing higher uptake capacity than birnessite, (2) Cr was co-sequestered with secondary Fe(III) (oxyhydr)oxides rather than adsorbing directly onto Mn oxides, and (3) synergistic Ni2+ isomorphic substitution and Fe(II)-driven Mn(III) reduction rearranged δ-MnO2 into a more stable hexagonal layered framework. Consequently, both δ-MnO2 and birnessite act as long-term Ni sinks, preventing Ni remobilization via desorption or diagenetic phase transitions. These findings support a proposed “spatial decoupling” OAE strategy, where olivine is pre-dissolved in land- or ship-based reactors to remove Cr via Fe co-precipitation. Subsequent discharge of the Ni-bearing alkaline effluent into shallow coastal regions allows benthic Mn oxides to scavenge Ni, reducing toxicity risks associated with direct mineral contact.</jats:p>

title:
Regional Impacts
of Unconventional Oil and Gas Operations
on Ozone and Air Toxics
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Unconventional oil and gas development (UOGD) has expanded over the past three decades and now accounts for most of U.S. oil and natural gas production. Although prior studies link local UOGD activity to health outcomes, they provide limited evidence directly attributing ambient pollutant levels to UOGD emissions. We address this gap by quantifying UOGD impacts on ozone and air toxics using the Community Multiscale Air Quality (CMAQ) model with the Integrated Source Apportionment Method (ISAM), enabling an explicit linkage between UOGD emissions and ambient concentrations. UOGD activities produce substantial local contributions to primary air toxics and continental-scale influences on ozone. Across CONUS, UOGD increases population-weighted annual averages of maximum daily average 8-h (MDA8) ozone, 1-h benzene, 1-h nitrogen dioxide (NO2), and 1-h formaldehyde (HCHO) concentrations by roughly 1 ppb, 1.1 ppt, 0.035 ppb, and 0.03 ppb, respectively. Annual maximum UOGD contributions to MDA8 ozone are about half of those from other anthropogenic sources. ISAM also reveals unexpectedly large UOGD-driven ozone enhancement (up to 4–5 ppb) in the Los Angeles region from Texas emissions, a feature less evident in brute-force sensitivity tests. These findings highlight the need to further examine interstate UOGD influences on nonattainment areas and source-impact quantification methods.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Renoxification of nitrate to reactive nitrogen species (RNS) can sustain atmospheric oxidant production. Because nitrate and light-absorbing brown carbon can coexist in biomass burning (BB) plumes, their photochemical interaction may alter RNS cycling. Furthermore, nitration of phenols in biomass burning organic aerosol (BBOA) can form nitrophenols, potentially increasing the warming effect of aged BBOA. Yet the mechanisms of renoxification and nitration in irradiated nitrate-BBOA mixtures remain poorly understood. We experimentally investigate these coupled processes over a wide range of fir-wood BBOA concentrations during aqueous nitrate photolysis (10 mM) under acidic conditions using H2SO4. At low BBOA concentration (TOCBBOA/NO3– ≤ 0.0036 mg L–1/mg L–1), the steady-state production rate of HONO (Pss_HONO) increased as BBOA concentration increased, reaching a maximum enhancement factor of 1.8 driven primarily by triplet-mediated photosensitized reduction of NO2 to HONO. At higher BBOA concentration (TOCBBOA/NO3– &gt; 0.0036 mg L–1/mg L–1), Pss_HONO progressively decreased and was nearly fully suppressed at TOCBBOA/NO3– = 0.7 mg L–1/mg L–1. This inhibition is attributed to reactions of aqueous HNO2/NO2 with phenols, accompanied by formation of nitrophenols. These findings point to a potentially overlooked daytime HONO source and an atmospheric source of nitrophenols, a key class of BrC chromophores, via photochemical interactions between nitrate photolysis and photosensitization of BBOA.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Caribbean countries bear a disproportionate burden of marine plastic pollution because of their small landmass, high population density, and insufficient waste management infrastructure. Many Caribbean nations depend on informal, unmanaged landfills, underscoring an urgent need for more resilient, sustainable systems. This perspective synthesizes existing data to map the region’s plastic waste landscape and leverages regional expertise to identify key research priorities. This work emerged from interdisciplinary international professionals and members of the CEPlaSt (circular economy for plastic sustainability) network. A major barrier to circularity is the lack of reliable data on waste composition and flows, alongside stark infrastructure disparities across the wider Caribbean region. Addressing these gaps through targeted investment and region-specific planning is essential to modernize waste systems, reduce plastic emissions, and advance a sustainable Caribbean plastic circular economy.</jats:p>

title:
Submarine Groundwater
Discharge Acts as a Significant
Vector for Coastal Organophosphate Esters: Joint Evidence from Pollution
Surveys and Radionuclide Analysis

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Organophosphate esters (OPEs) are ubiquitous marine contaminants that raise global concern. While surface inputs are well-studied, the role of subsurface transport remains poorly constrained. Submarine groundwater discharge (SGD) drives seawater-groundwater interactions, yet its impact on OPEs behavior remains overlooked. This study comprehensively investigates the distribution, transport property and sources of OPEs from coastal groundwater to seawater in the Beibu Gulf, China. No statistically significant difference in Σ19OPEs levels was found between groundwater and tidal flat porewater, while both matrices exhibited significantly higher levels than seawater. The high compositional similarity, strong correlations (p &lt; 0.01) and PCA overlap of OPEs in different waters, as well as their shared source profiles indicated the transport potential of OPEs from groundwater to seawater. Multiple statistical modeling integrating OPEs, environmental factors and DOM components reveals the land-to-sea transport pathways and biogeochemical processes of OPEs via SGD. Furthermore, radon isotope analysis verified the presence of SGD, offering evidence for SGD-mediated OPE transport. For the first time, this work integrates pollutant investigation, multiple statistical analysis, and radionuclide tracing, to identify SGD as a previously underestimated vector of coastal OPEs and elucidates its potential transport mechanisms, providing crucial support for integrated land-sea management and risk assessment.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Evidence linking PM2.5 exposure to allergic symptoms remains limited and inconsistent, partly because most studies rely on mass-based metrics alone. We conducted a population-based study among 131,346 children aged 6–18 years in six cities of Guangdong, China, to compare associations of PM2.5 mass concentration, oxidative potential (OP), and chemical components (metals, carbonaceous components, and ions) with rhinitis, rhinoconjunctivitis, and eczema symptoms. OP was assessed using the dithiothreitol assay and expressed as volume-normalized (DTTv) and mass-normalized (DTTm) metrics. PM2.5 mass and OP were generally positively associated with the three allergy-related symptoms. OP, particularly DTTm, provided more consistent and robust evidence of associations across outcomes than PM2.5 mass, supported by lower AIC/BIC values and greater stability in two-pollutant models. Single-component and mixture analyses indicated that multiple PM2.5 constituents contributed to allergy-related symptoms, and OP may partly explain the associations of Co, OC, Cu, and Hg, with the largest estimated indirect proportion reaching 36.2% for OC and rhinoconjunctivitis symptoms through DTTm. These findings suggest that OP captures health-relevant characteristics beyond particle mass and may serve as a complementary exposure indicator for understanding childhood symptoms of allergic diseases.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Nitrogen-containing organic compounds (NOCs) are ubiquitous in the troposphere and contribute to the reactive nitrogen cycle and aerosol light absorption, yet their formation mechanisms remain unclear, especially in polluted regions. Here, we characterized NOCs in PM2.5 during winter haze in the North China Plain (NCP), with a comparison to those in the Sichuan Basin (ScB). Reduced-nitrogen NOCs (Re-NOCs) accounted for 40% of organics detected in the ESI+ mode, highlighting their importance within atmospheric NOCs. Compared to dry haze (DH) in NCP, high-molecular-weight (HMW, m/z &gt; 250) Re-NOCs in humid haze (HH) were enhanced, which positively correlated with NH4+ and the mass ratio of aqueous-phase secondary organic aerosols to total water-soluble organic aerosols, along with increases in aliphatic chain length and molecular unsaturation, indicating carbonyl-amino-driven oligomerization and cyclization. Aliphatic Re-NOCs dominated the Re-NOCs during HH, together with strong correlations of a typical NOC oligomer (C8H13N3O2) with water-soluble organic nitrogen and HMW Re-NOCs, further suggesting oligomerization as a key formation pathway for NOCs. We found that stronger aerosol acidity and higher temperature favored oligomerization of Re-NOCs compared to cyclization, resulting in enhanced C8H13N3O2 in ScB relative to that in NCP. Our work revealed oligomerization as a critical mechanism shaping the NOC composition, particularly HMW species.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Technetium-99 is a long-lived, high-yield fission product whose solubility is controlled by redox conditions. Here, to explore targeted effluent treatment approaches, pertechnetate (Tc(VII)O4–) reductive retention as Tc(IV) during coprecipitation of Fe(II)-doped Ni–Al–CO3 layered double hydroxide (LDH) was investigated. During LDH formation via base addition to an acidic Ni2+, Al3+, Fe2+, and Tc(VII)O4– bearing solution, there was essentially complete TcO4– removal at low (9.6 Bq/mL) and high (2.9 kBq/mL) concentrations. Characterization of experiments using X-ray diffraction, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) confirmed that, during base titration, a two-stage process occurred, with Al3+ forming amorphous Al (hydr)oxide between pH 4 and 6 in the first stage, followed by hydrolysis of Fe2+/Ni2+ and formation of LDH particles between pH 6 and 9 in stage two. During the first stage, TcO4– was removed from solution, and XAS confirmed it was reduced to Tc(IV) by Fe(II) associated with the amorphous Al (hydr)oxide, forming hydrous Tc(IV)O2-like chains on the Al (hydr)oxide surface. During the second stage, XAS showed that Tc(IV) was incorporated within the newly formed LDH structure. Overall, these data provide novel insights into the application of LDH formation in Tc sequestration and suggest novel effluent treatment pathways to produce an inorganic solid.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Elevated arsenic concentrations in groundwater pose health risks. Geogenic arsenic contamination is driven by biogeochemical mobilization and groundwater dynamics. Intensive pumping can initially exacerbate contamination by drawing arsenic or mobilizing organic matter into aquifers, but over longer time scales may also promote dilution and flushing in some settings. To better understand the mechanisms controlling arsenic concentrations, we examined changes over two decades in Hanoi (Vietnam), a hotspot of geogenic arsenic contamination and groundwater pumping. Arsenic concentrations from 470 wells sampled in the year 2000 were compared with 434 wells sampled in the same area in 2013 and 2023. Median concentrations declined from 14 to 8 μg/L between 2000 and 2023, while mean concentrations and the proportion of high-arsenic wells (&gt;100 μg/L) remained similar. Using hydrochemical and groundwater-level data, CatBoost models combined with SHAP analysis assessed changes in predictor importance. In 2000, arsenic was more strongly associated with redox predictors, whereas groundwater-level predictors became more important in 2023. Within wells used to evaluate groundwater-level change (n = 251), larger decadal declines were associated with lower arsenic concentrations (median = 31 μg/L) than wells without declines (median = 120 μg/L). We hypothesize a decadal mechanism shift, from redox to hydrological controls, particularly driving arsenic declines.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Long-chain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in industrial wastewater are a significant source of PFAS contamination. Anion exchange resin (AER) adsorption is an advantageous technology for PFAS removal, but existing AERs suffer from limited selectivity. In this study, our synthesized novel macroporous AERs with asymmetric long-chain amine groups, MP-(12–1–1) and MP-(16–1–1), exhibited a unique floating behavior on the water surface after drying and achieved significantly enhanced PFAS removal from chromium-plating wastewater, with the gas–liquid interface playing a critical role. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed that the rough surfaces and hydrophobic functional groups of the dry MP-(12–1–1) and MP-(16–1–1) enable them to maintain the Cassie wetting state in water without transitioning to the Wenzel state, thereby forming a stable gas–liquid interface. The gas–liquid interface exhibited adsorption free energies reaching −7.6 to −9.5 kcal/mol for long-chain PFAS, increasing the selectivity of the floating macroporous AERs for various long-chain PFAS by 6–81 times. This provides a new approach for the efficient removal of long-chain PFAS and offers new insights for the design of selective adsorbents based on the gas–liquid interface.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Ocean acidification (OA) poses a significant threat to marine organisms, yet its effects on fish sensory systems remain poorly understood. This study investigated the effects of elevated pCO2 on olfactory function in the large yellow croaker, Larimichthys crocea. Elevated pCO2 reduced peripheral olfactory sensitivity, as evidenced by suppressed electro-olfactogram responses. This impairment was accompanied by epithelial disorganization, cellular damage, increased apoptosis in the olfactory epithelium, and reduced expression of olfactory neuron markers. In vitro analyses using a selected recombinant L. crocea odorant receptor LORA1–1 showed that acidified pH altered its physicochemical properties and odorant-specific receptor–ligand interaction dynamics. OA also downregulated genes associated with odorant receptor expression, G protein-mediated signaling, calcium-related transduction, and neuronal maturation. Telencephalic responses included altered ion-transport ATPase activities, histopathological abnormalities, oxidative stress, enhanced apoptotic activity, and reduced neuropeptide Y expression. Transcriptomic and proteomic analyses further identified telencephalic molecular changes associated with altered neuroactive ligand–receptor interaction, calcium signaling, glutathione metabolism, apoptosis, mitophagy, MAPK signaling, and olfactory transduction. Our findings suggest that epithelial injury, altered odorant recognition, and disrupted peripheral signaling contribute to OA-induced olfactory impairment in L. crocea, with potential consequences for migration and reproduction that depend on olfactory cues.</jats:p>

title:
Submicroscale
and
Molecular Insights into Labile Organic
Matter Transformation and Sequestration at Newly Formed Iron Minerals–Water
Interfaces during O2-Mediated Fe(II) Oxidation

affiliation.name: Sichuan Forestry Survey and Design Institute Co., Ltd. , , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Abiotic Fe(II) oxidation and subsequent precipitation are key pathways for controlling labile organic matter (OM) dynamics in O2-perturbed subsurface environments, yet the underlying coupling mechanisms remain poorly understood. Herein, OM transformation and sequestration during O2-mediated heterogeneous Fe(II) oxidation were evaluated at neutral pH across various C/Fe ratios. Increasing C/Fe ratios impeded Fe(II) oxidation but enhanced the level of reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Despite efficient sequestration, the OM immobilization efficiency varied with C/Fe ratios, with a minor fraction of OM being oxidized by ROS. Higher C/Fe ratios promoted ferrihydrite formation but inhibited its transformation into lepidocrocite, forming mineral-organic composites constituted by Fe–O cores and edge-/corner-sharing Fe–Fe shells. A direct visualization at submicroscale revealed heterogeneous spatial distributions of different organo functional groups on newly formed Fe mineral surfaces, reflecting OM selective immobilization. Newly formed Fe minerals preferentially immobilized high-molecular-weight compounds and those with more oxygenated or highly unsaturated structures, with stronger molecular fractionation at higher C/Fe ratios. Molecular-level analysis revealed that a lower C/Fe ratio promoted the conversion of phenols to quinones, aromatic ring opening, and carboxylation of aromatic substituents but inhibited polymerization of phenolic substances. Collectively, these findings deepen our knowledge of heterogeneous Fe mineral formation coupled with OM sequestration and transformation, advancing our understanding of Fe and C geochemical cycling in oxic soils and sediments.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Nanoplastics (NPs) and antibiotics co-occur in wastewater systems, but how NP size influences antibiotic biodegradation by specialized degraders remains unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of europium-doped polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs; PS20 and PS100) on sulfadiazine biodegradation by Arthrobacter sp. strain D2. Modified Gompertz modeling revealed two contrasting inhibition regimes. For PS100, inhibition was dominated by lag-phase prolongation, with no detectable sulfadiazine removal over 48 h at a PS100 concentration of 100 mg L–1. In contrast, PS20 reduced the maximum sulfadiazine degradation rate by ∼40% while causing only minor changes in lag time, indicating rate-dominated inhibition. Quartz crystal microbalance with dissipation monitoring at a model sulfadiazine-enriched interface showed that PS100 markedly reduced the deposition of NP-pre-exposed cells, whereas PS20 only partially impaired adhesion. Transmission electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy further revealed intracellular accumulation of PS20, whereas PS100 remained predominantly extracellular. Phase-specific physiological measurements and transcriptomics suggested that PS20 induced oxidative-stress responses associated with reduced sulfadiazine biodegradation rates, whereas PS100 elicited dose-dependent transcriptional changes during lag-phase extension. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that nanoplastics impair antibiotic attenuation through distinct size-dependent mechanisms involving interface-associated constraints and intracellular interference, highlighting particle size as a key determinant of antibiotic fate in plastic-contaminated wastewater environments.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Organophosphate esters (OPEs) are ubiquitous indoors, posing threats to public health. However, limited information on both the permissible levels and environmental behavior makes global regulation challenging. Herein, a closed-loop mechanistic framework, termed the Indoor OPE Source Identification and Exposure Direct Assessment (IOSIEDA) model, tracing the cause-and-effect chain from OPE source contents to health impacts, was developed to forecast indoor OPE emissions and fate, rapidly screen risks, prioritize high-risk OPE-material combinations, and back-calculate risk-based threshold contents (RTCs). Model evaluation via Monte Carlo simulation and a residential case study revealed a total Σ13OPEs influx of ∼2053 μg day–1, predominantly originating from indoor source emissions (99.4%), with 95% loss via air exchange. Notably, the IOSIEDA model back-calculated the RTCs within a risk-based framework built upon the source-specific relationship between OPE contents and emission characteristics, developing health-prevention-oriented thresholds for a set of unregulated OPEs across five types of understudied source materials. Global application across 16 countries provided emissions and an RTC database for indoor OPEs, filling in the missing values for global national thresholds of OPEs in specific source materials. Total residential OPE emissions were estimated at ∼74,500 kg yr–1; Asia constitutes the major emission region, and RTCs exhibit distinct regional disparities across continents.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Ambient air pollution may impair childhood neurodevelopment, but sensitive windows, mediating pathways, and the neurodevelopmental benefits of air-quality interventions remain unclear. In this prospective birth cohort of 3575 mother–child pairs in Wuhan, China (2014–2019), neurodevelopment at age two was assessed using the Bayley Scales, and cord serum sex steroids were measured in 897 pairs. Associations of air pollution exposure from preconception through the second postnatal year with neurodevelopment at age two and potential sex-steroid mediation were evaluated. Target trial emulation (TTE) was used to estimate neurodevelopmental differences associated with China’s 2013–2017 air-quality intervention. Most air pollutants were inversely associated with neurodevelopment across multiple exposure windows, with associations generally strongest during the first postnatal year. Mediation analyses suggested that androstenedione mediated 5–12% of associations between specific preconception/prenatal air pollutant exposures and Psychomotor Development Index, although inverse-probability-weighted indirect effects were no longer statistically significant. TTE suggested significant neurodevelopmental benefits following the air-quality intervention, with Mental Development Index and Psychomotor Development Index improving by 7.27 and 6.41 points in the later policy-period group, respectively. These findings support more stringent long-term air pollution standards and sustained air-quality interventions to protect child neurodevelopment.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Granular activated carbon (GAC) is widely used to remove perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) from contaminated water, yet its sustainable regeneration remains challenging. Solvent-based regeneration preserves the carbon matrix but may shift environmental burdens toward solvent production, chemical use, energy demand, and downstream waste management. Here we present a life cycle assessment (LCA) of PFOS-laden GAC regeneration using deionized water (GAC-WR) and ethanol (GAC-ER). We identify electricity-driven elution and downstream incineration as the dominant environmental hotspots across 18 midpoint impact categories. Selected chemical-assisted configurations (NaOH-modified water and HCl-modified ethanol) improved regeneration efficiency and reduced environmental impacts under the evaluated conditions by reducing virgin GAC supplementation. An industrial-scale model incorporating equipment upscaling and thermal integration further mitigated laboratory-specific energy overestimation. Compared with the corresponding baseline scenarios using the global electricity mix, hydropower-based electricity reduces global warming potential to 3.30 and 8.26 kg CO2e kg–1 for GAC-WR and GAC-ER, respectively, while increasing life-cycle water consumption to 230% and 266% of the respective baselines. This cross-category burden shift demonstrates that reducing climate impacts does not necessarily reduce the broader life-cycle environmental footprint. Overall, sustainable solvent-based GAC regeneration requires balancing regeneration efficiency, energy supply, chemical inputs, solvent recovery, and management of PFAS-containing wastes.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), a transformation product of the tire rubber antioxidant 6PPD, is an emerging contaminant known for its acute toxicity to certain salmonids. However, its potential impacts on aquatic communities remain poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, 6PPD-Q-spiked limnocorrals were deployed in a natural boreal lake, and water chemistry, phytoplankton, zooplankton, and benthic invertebrate communities were assessed over 28 days following a single pulse exposure (0–100 μg/L) simulating stormwater runoff. Waterborne 6PPD-Q concentrations declined by 80–99% by the end of the study, with no detectable effects on water chemistry or aquatic communities. Temporal changes in chlorophyll-a concentrations and zooplankton abundance were attributed to seasonal dynamics rather than 6PPD-Q exposure, and benthic invertebrate community composition remained unchanged. Concurrently, wild-spawned fathead minnow (Pimephales promelas) embryos were exposed to 6PPD-Q-spiked water collected from the limnocorrals. Larval survival declined significantly at 100 μg/L, with altered hatch timing and sublethal effects including reduced growth, changes in eye, yolk sac, and pericardial areas, and altered energy allocation. These effects occurred at 10.6–22.4 μg/L and above, concentrations that exceed those so far reported in surface waters and stormwater by approximately an order of magnitude. Collectively, this study provides the first field-scale assessment of 6PPD-Q effects on aquatic communities and early life-stage fish. Environmental Significance. This study provides the first field-scale assessment of 6PPD-Q impacts on freshwater communities. While broad aquatic communities appeared resilient to short-term exposure scenarios, early life stages of fish responded at concentrations above those currently reported in the environment, identifying developmental end points that warrant attention when assessing the risks of tire-derived contaminants in freshwater ecosystems.</jats:p>

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Fouling remains the key barrier to durable membrane operation, against which electrochemical processes offer a promising fouling control strategy. However, the performance of an anodic membrane under anaerobic conditions exhibits significant instability, the mechanism of which remains unclear and represents a critical knowledge gap. This study systematically investigated the response of membrane fouling evolution to gradient electric fields within anodic membranes. A distinct threshold behavior of electric field strength on membrane fouling was observed, with a system-dependent threshold occurring between 0.7 and 1.0 V. Following an initial fouling layer, subthreshold fields (≤0.7 V) exacerbated fouling accumulation, whereas supra-threshold fields (≥1.0 V) slowed down membrane fouling development. Comprehensive analysis revealed that surpassing critical field strength enhanced anodic electron-accepting capacity, likely facilitating microbial extracellular electron release and alleviating reductive pressure. This triggered a nonlinear, threshold-dependent metabolic switch from biosynthesis-dominated to catabolism-enhanced pathways, coupled with quorum quenching that inhibited biofilm maturation. These synergistic transitions underpinned the fouling reversal. This work advances the understanding of anaerobic-anodic membrane fouling from an empirical observation into a threshold-governed electrochemical–microbial switching process, thereby providing the scientific foundation for harnessing this interplay to achieve durable and efficient operation in anaerobic wastewater treatment and resource recovery systems.</jats:p>

title:

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Atmospheric nitrogen deposition in China is driven not only by local emissions but also by global economic demand and transboundary atmospheric transport. Unraveling these dual influences is critical for effective environmental governance. Here, we integrate an economic-emission analysis with a high-resolution atmospheric chemical transport model to quantify, for the first time, the distinct roles of domestic consumption, international trade, and atmospheric transport in shaping China’s nitrogen deposition patterns. We find that domestic consumption is the dominant contributor, responsible for 67.6% of the total deposition, involving a substantial interprovincial transfer of emissions from affluent coastal provinces to less developed inland regions. International trade attributes 7.8% of China’s deposition to foreign consumption, primarily driven by demand from the USA and Western Europe. In contrast, trans-national atmospheric transport directly accounts for 12.8%, with a disproportionately high impact on ecologically sensitive western China. Natural sources contribute the remaining 11.8%. Our results reveal a complex web of drivers extending beyond China’s borders. Mitigating nitrogen deposition, therefore, requires moving beyond local emission controls to embrace consumption-based accountability and enhanced international cooperation on both trade and atmospheric pollution to protect vulnerable ecosystems.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Dissolved organic matter (DOM) in aquatic ecosystems is crucial to climate, water quality, and water sanitation. However, little is known about how photochemical and biological processes interact to regulate the cycling of DOM in water environments. Here, we investigate the photobiochemical processing of different molecular weight (MW) fractions of aquatic DOM by incubating them with microbes in the dark and light/dark cycling environments via microcosm experiments. Light exposure has distinct effects on the medium (MMW; 1–20 kDa) and low (LMW; &lt;1 kDa) MW fractions and can enrich photoautotrophic bacteria and taxa that could benefit the utilization of aromatic compounds. The decay of the MMW fraction displays the highest light sensitivity, with light increasing the net depletion of tannin- and condensed aromatic-like molecules and production of labile substrates (e.g., protein-like) from photoautotrophic bacteria. In contrast, the net decomposition of the LMW fraction is the least promoted by light exposure, as light induces the net production of complex aromatic molecules that are more persistent. Our findings provide new insights into the photobiochemical and molecular mechanisms underlying the ecological impacts of aquatic DOM and their relevance for wider processes.</jats:p>

title:
Selective
Oxidation
of Sulfoxide to Sulfone in Chloride/Peroxymonosulfate
Systems: Reassessing a Diagnostic Probe for High-Valent Metal-Oxo
Identification
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The selective oxidation of sulfoxides to sulfones, particularly using methyl phenyl sulfoxide (PMSO), has been widely adopted for over a decade as a diagnostic method for high-valent metal-oxo (HVMO) species in advanced oxidation processes (AOPs). Here, we demonstrate that this transformation proceeds efficiently via non-HVMO pathways in metal-free systems, challenging the probe’s specificity. Using the chloride/peroxymonosulfate (Cl−/PMS) system as a model, PMSO is converted to methyl phenyl sulfone (PMSO2) with high selectivity (83.5%−98.7%) across pH 3.5−11. Kinetic, isotopic, and computational analyses reveal a pH-dependent mechanistic switch for the high-yield transformation of PMSO to PMSO2. Under acidic conditions, Cl2/HOCl generated from the two-electron oxidation of Cl− by HSO5− through nucleophilic addition mediate oxygen-atom transfer from water via a chlorosulfonium cation intermediate, with Cl2 dominating PMSO selective oxidation (kapp = 1.58 × 106 M−1 s−1; 47.91 M−1 s−1 for HOCl). Under alkaline conditions, nucleophilic attack by SO52− formed via PMS hydrolysis becomes predominant (16.38 M−1 s−1). The reaction kinetics are linearly dependent on Cl− concentration, and similar selective oxidation is observed in other metal-free AOPs (e.g., base/PMS, HCO3−/PMS, and Cl−/peracetic acid). Our findings necessitate reassessing the sulfoxide probe’s specificity for HVMO identification in PMS-based systems containing chloride or alkalinity, and underscore the imperative for rigorous mechanistic validation in water treatment.</jats:p>

title:
Perspectives and
Mitigation Methods for Underappreciated
Amine Escape from CO2 Desorption
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Amine-based CO2 capture is increasingly limited by amine escape and aerosol emissions that drive solvent loss and secondary pollution. Research has focused on the absorber, leaving the desorption section─where intensive CO2 release, water-vapor entrainment, and rapid cooling coincide─overlooked as an escape source. Here, we combine molecular dynamics simulations with bench-scale experiments to resolve the mechanism and control of amine escape during CO2 desorption. Counter to absorber-side expectations, a CO2-rich atmosphere suppresses rather than promotes aerosol nucleation: elevated CO2 competitively disrupts the H2O–H2O hydrogen-bond network stabilizing water-centered nuclei, with stable clusters essentially absent at 75 vol % CO2. New aerosol formation is thus favored near the low-CO2 reboiler outlet, while cooling in the upper column grows preexisting aerosols. Measurements revealed an 82% decrease in the total amine concentration along the column, consistent with the descending rich solvent acting as an important amine sink, while preexisting aerosols continued to grow in the upper section. Guided by this mechanism, a combined mitigation strategy is proposed: a low-volatility solvent formulation lowered aerosol by 66% relative to MEA, increasing the rich-solvent CO2 loading offered a favorable trade-off, and upstream scrubbing–condensation captured residual species. Together, these measures reduced amine escape by over 99% (to &lt;1.4 ppm) while increasing CO2 product purity. By reframing the desorber as a key emission unit, these results support strategies for reducing desorber-side amine and aerosol emissions.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Five decades of research on disinfection byproducts (DBPs) reveals only the tip of the iceberg, with humus as their primary precursor. Here, we identified 15 halogenated nucleosides (HNSs) as new DBPs originating from biological materials in drinking water. A nationwide survey across China revealed that their individual detection frequencies ranged from 87% to 100%, with the maximum concentration reaching 141 ng/L. Two quantitative structure–activity relationship (QSAR) models were developed based on the cytotoxicity and genotoxicity data, with dipole moment (μ) and sum of the degree of valence (SVDe) as key cytotoxicity descriptors, and molar refractivity (R) together with number of H-bond donors (NHD) for genotoxicity. Integrated concentration and toxicity data revealed that halogenated (deoxy)cytidines and halogenated (deoxy)adenosines warrant priority regulatory consideration. The concentrations of HNSs were positively correlated with both pH (r = 0.6, P = 0.0005) and residual chlorine (r = 0.5, P = 0.0095) of drinking water samples, which may be related to local precipitation, temperature, and economic development. This study expands the scope of DBP research beyond humus-derived DBPs to biomolecule-derived ones.</jats:p>

title:
Unveiling Whole
Water Neurotoxicity through Sensitive
Electrophysiological Functional Profiling: Beyond Conventional Morphological
Metrics
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Neuroactive contaminants typically coexist as complex mixtures in aquatic ecosystems, exerting deleterious effects through combined exposures. However, current assessment approaches based on morphological endpoints (e.g., neurite outgrowth) lack sufficient sensitivity to capture functional neurotoxicity of these mixtures. To address this gap, this study establishes in vitro functional neurotoxicity testing (iFNT), an ultrasensitive bioassay leveraging high-density microelectrode arrays to profile cortical network electrophysiology. Validated using reference toxicants, their mixture, and whole water samples, iFNT achieves 5- to 500-fold higher sensitivity than the neurite outgrowth assay. This heightened sensitivity enables clearer discrimination of functional phenotypes for both individual compounds at environmentally relevant concentrations (10–8 M) and whole water samples without preconcentration, providing a powerful tool for evaluating real-world neurotoxic risks. Alarmingly, conventional monitoring indicators exhibited a pronounced mismatch with iFNT profiles across wastewater treatment stages, demonstrating that seemingly acceptable routine readings masked the persistence of latent neurotoxicity. This study challenges morphology-based paradigms, revealing that accurate whole water risk assessment necessitates integrating functional biological endpoints into future monitoring frameworks.</jats:p>

title:
Bromine Monoxide
Radical Likely Dominates Dimethylsulfide
Oxidation before the Springtime Onset of Arctic Ice Melt

affiliation.name: Rosenstiel School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Earth Science , , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>To understand the atmospheric fate of dimethylsulfide (DMS) during the Arctic spring-to-summer transition, we measured volatile methylated sulfur (VMS) species, including DMS and DMS-derived oxidation products, dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and dimethylsulfone (DMSO2), in the Fram Strait during May and June of 2023. Elevated DMSO contributions to VMS accompany depleted O3, high surface albedo, and air temperatures &lt; 0 °C in air masses influenced by snow-covered sea-ice regions, suggesting that BrO•-initiated oxidation dominated DMS loss prior to the onset of sea-ice melt. In GEOS-Chem simulations, BrO• is the dominant oxidant for DMS, but modeled BrO• concentrations from sea-salt debromination alone are too low to replicate observed O3, DMSO, and DMSO2, suggesting a missing source of reactive bromine from sunlit saline snow. BrO•-initiated oxidation reduces the DMS lifetime and oxidizes DMS through methanesulfinic acid (MSIA) more quickly in the gas phase and in higher yields compared to •OH-initiated oxidation alone. Once melt onset begins and snowpack-driven halogen activation shuts off, •OH oxidation likely dominates Arctic DMS oxidation. Our observations highlight the seasonal variability of halogen oxidation impacting sulfur species in the Arctic marine region, which are likely to change as the sea-ice extent decreases and the melt season in the Arctic lengthens.</jats:p>

title:
Atmospheric
Removal
of Nitrous Oxide: Approaches and
Feasibility
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Nitrous oxide (N2O) is the third-largest contributor to anthropogenic greenhouse gas forcing and the dominant anthropogenic ozone-depleting emission. While mitigation can flatten emissions, there is no clear pathway to eliminate residual emissions from agriculture and other diffuse sources, a key challenge for climate stabilization. The potential role of atmospheric removal has not been holistically assessed, yet N2O’s high potency and long atmospheric lifetime indicate the potential for a durable climate benefit. This review synthesizes emerging approaches for atmospheric N2O removal, organized by reaction mechanism (thermal destruction and thermocatalysis, photolysis, gas-phase radical reactions, photocatalysis, and biological reduction) and deployment format (closed versus open system). Each is evaluated for technical efficacy, climate viability, environmental and social viability, and economic plausibility using lower-bound cost models. No approach yet satisfies all four: gas-phase radical reactors are precluded by their kinetics, thermocatalytic and photocatalytic reactors require ten- to hundred-fold performance gains, and open-system approaches have the lowest cost floors but face the greatest measurement and governance challenges. These results identify the performance thresholds and broader constraints that govern feasibility across pathways, providing a foundation for a research agenda and for assessing the role of N2O removal alongside emissions mitigation.</jats:p>

title:
Toward Rational
Design of Low-Salt-Rejection Reverse
Osmosis for Minimal and Zero Liquid Discharge

affiliation.name: China University of Mining and Technology (Beijing) , , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Low-salt-rejection reverse osmosis (LSRRO) has emerged as a promising technology for concentrating high-salinity brines in minimal- and zero-liquid-discharge (MLD/ZLD) applications. However, rational LSRRO design remains hindered by uncertainties about how existing modeling frameworks should be interpreted and applied. In this Perspective, we critically examine the limitations of process modeling and module-scale analysis in LSRRO design. Conventional process models can yield misleading predictions for spiral-wound LSRRO modules because the stagewise concentration cutoff embedded in these models is based on the cumulative permeate composition rather than the local permeate conditions that govern water transport. Experimental results and local transport calculations show that the brine concentration in spiral-wound LSRRO stages is not constrained by a fixed thermodynamic concentration cutoff. Nevertheless, standalone process models remain inherently limited in assessing practical feasibility because they do not resolve kinetic constraints, such as declining water flux along the module. Module-scale analysis is therefore essential for linking local transport behavior to practical design metrics, including membrane area requirements, productivity, and achievable brine concentration. However, its predictive accuracy is constrained because transport parameters derived from conventional local transport models vary with salinity, which challenges their use as constants across the module. This Perspective therefore highlights the need for condition-dependent and experimentally validated local transport descriptions to enable rational LSRRO design for future MLD/ZLD applications.</jats:p>

title:
Dynamic Nature of
Soil Iron Minerals: Recent Advances

affiliation.name: Netherlands Organization of Applied Scientific Research (TNO) , , Princetonlaan 6 , ,

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Iron plays a central role in defining the redox and surface chemical environment of soils and sediments, by mediating the behavior of nutrients, pollutants, and carbon compounds. However, the mechanisms that drive dynamic changes in Fe speciation and mineral composition can be difficult to trace. Over three decades, technical advances in spectroscopy and theoretical modeling techniques have revealed detailed mechanisms of Fe mineral recrystallization and transformation. Here, we provide a perspective on the application of iron isotopic tracers to the development of atomic-scale mechanistic understanding of Fe mineral dynamics. We review key milestones in the advancement of 57Fe tracers coupled with 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy and draw links between the understanding of Fe dynamics with 57Fe tracers and biogeochemical cycling of other elements in soils and sediments. Iron isotopes are increasingly used in Fe biogeochemistry research, and our analysis will point out unique opportunities offered by 57Fe tracers to unravel important questions in soil biogeochemistry today.</jats:p>

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>The effect of prenatal organophosphate esters (OPEs) exposure on offspring reproductive development and the potential role of the placenta remain unclear. We investigated the associations of prenatal OPE exposure with the second-to-fourth digit ratio (2D:4D) and the mediating role of placental DNA methylation (DNAm) levels of PPAR pathway genes. Maternal urine OPE metabolites at 12–16 gestational weeks were measured. Placental DNAm levels at birth and children’s 2D:4D at ages 4 and 6 years were assessed. Multiple linear regression, BKMR, and causal mediation analyses were applied. We observed associations between prenatal exposure to BBOEP, BEHP, DBP, and DPP and increased 2D:4D in boys, whereas DBP and DCP were associated with decreased 2D:4D in girls. BKMR identified alkyl-OPEs, particularly BBOEP, as the primary contributors in boys. Moreover, hypermethylation of RXRA, ACAA1, and ACADM was associated with decreased 2D:4D in all populations. In girls, the associations among higher OPE exposure, increased ACAA1 methylation, and lower 2D:4D suggested a potential mediation pathway, while the mediation effects were not statistically significant. These findings suggest sex-specific associations between prenatal OPE exposure and 2D:4D. The potential role of placental PPAR-related DNAm in these associations warrants further investigation.</jats:p>

title: Medium-Entropy LDH-Driven Electronic Coupling of MnO x for Preferential Oxidation of Formaldehyde
items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Preferential oxidation of formaldehyde (HCHO) in natural gas engine exhaust is pivotal to prevent NH3–SCR catalyst deactivation and inhibit highly toxic hydrogen cyanide (HCN) formation. Although manganese-based catalysts exhibit prominent activity for HCHO oxidation, complete mineralization is still hindered by poor electron-transfer efficiency and insufficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Herein, we fabricate hierarchical medium-entropy LDH nanoflower-anchored MnOx catalysts (MnO2@NiMgAl-MELH) via a facile in situ growth strategy, enabling 100% mineralization of HCHO at room temperature. Structural characterizations and DFT calculations verify that Ni–Mn electronic coupling optimizes the electronic structure, facilitates charge transfer, reduces oxygen vacancy formation energy, and boosts O2 and H2O activation to generate abundant ROS (O2–, O22–, and surface −OH). Furthermore, in situ DRIFTS confirms that ROS synergistically accelerate HCHO and formate intermediate oxidation, achieving complete mineralization of HCHO. This work develops a low-cost and high-performance catalyst for HCHO preferential oxidation and offers a broadly applicable strategy for air pollutant purification.</jats:p>
